title: The regular-module normalization of the sectionwise encoding
statement: Let B be a commutative topological ring and eR a unital isomorphism from its sheafified constant ULift B ring at the profinite point to its continuous-function condensed ring. Let G be an equivalence from internal ULift B modules in abelian groups to ordinary modules, with literal equality hG of their forgetful functors [def-weil-pbc-common-finite-discrete-encoding]. Assume its regular-module comparison is an isomorphism whose underlying map is the component of hG. For every scheme X for which forgetting ordinary modules to abelian groups preserves sheafification, write F for the inverse common coefficient equivalence and u for its sectionwise underlying-sheaf comparison. There is an isomorphism i from F of the regular internal coefficient module to the ordinary constant ULift B module [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-finite-realization]. The composite of u inverse, the underlying map of i, and the constant-module forgetful comparison is exactly the inverse of finiteDiscreteSchemeRingIso B X eR.

proof.text: Restrict the regular coefficient module along the fixed scheme ring isomorphism. Its inverse gives an explicit regular-module isomorphism; the multiplication equation follows from multiplicativity and the ring inverse identities.

At the terminal pro-etale object, take the component of the module-localization adjunction unit and identify the regular presheaf module with the regular abelian internal module. Apply G and the supplied normalized regular-module comparison. The constant-sheaf adjunction extends this section map to a morphism q from the constant A-module to the encoded regular sheaf. Naturality of the forgetful comparison identifies its underlying section with the constant-section unit. The constant-sheaf counit-forgetting identity and adjunction triangle give the exact underlying normalization of q.

The normalized underlying map of q is an isomorphism, so reflection of isomorphisms by forgetting modules makes q invertible. Compose its inverse with the encoding of the regular-module ring comparison. Naturality of the underlying comparison and cancellation yield precisely the inverse scheme coefficient-ring map.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof using the module-localization unit at the terminal object, the constant-sheaf counit comparison, and the adjunction triangle. No new sorry is used by this theorem.

theorem finiteEncoding_unitComparison
    (hregular : ∃ j : G.obj (Mod.regular (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B))) ≅
        ModuleCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B) (ULift.{u + 1} B),
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) Ab.{u + 1}).map j.hom =
        (eqToIso hG).hom.app (Mod.regular (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B))))
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [(Scheme.ProEt.topology X).PreservesSheafification
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) Ab.{u + 1})] :
    ∃ i : (finiteEncoding B eR G hG X).obj
        (Mod.regular (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) X)) ≅
        (constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B))).obj
            (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B) (ULift.{u + 1} B)),
      (finiteEncodingUnderlying B eR G hG X).inv.app
          (Mod.regular (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) X)) ≫
        (sheafCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) Ab.{u + 1})).map i.hom ≫
        ((constantCommuteCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) Ab.{u + 1})).app
            (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B) (ULift.{u + 1} B))).hom =
      (finiteDiscreteSchemeRingIso B X eR).inv
